newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK C.BANK SETS 1-DAY REV REPO TENDER FOR THURS.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK C.BANK SETS 1-DAY REV REPO TENDER FOR THURS.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said on Thursday it had set a tender for a one-day securities reverse repurchase for 10 a.m. (0900 GMT), offering to sterilise an unspecified volume of market liquidity.
The NBS said in a statement that the American-style tender would have no fixed minimum rate.

According to official NBS figures, the Slovak banking sector is short of liquidity, with banks' minimum reserve demands fulfilled at 98.29 percent as of Wednesday, after 95.83 percent the previous day.

Slovak interbank money market rates rose sharply last week due to a liquidity crunch, attracting some $150-200 million in foreign short-term capital, the bulk of which is expected to enter the market this week.
The NBS holds tenders on a daily basis, if needed, instead of quoting securities repo and reverse repo rates.
